description: Run one SOQL query against Salesforce and return a page of records. Pass `soql` such as "SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:30". When `done` is false, call again with `next_cursor` as `cursor` to read the next page; the query text is ignored on those calls.

soql.description: The SOQL statement to run, for example "SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 50".

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` from a previous call. Reads the next page and ignores `soql`.

records.description: The page of records, untouched, including Salesforce's own `attributes` block.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to read the next page. Null when the query is finished.

total_size.description: How many records the whole query matches, not just this page.

quirks.why_execute_and_not_http: Two reasons a declarative http mapping cannot cover: the call host is per connection (see salesforce_api.ts), and the path changes shape between the first page (/query?q=) and the next ones (/query/{locator}).
quirks.cursor_is_a_locator_not_a_url: Salesforce returns nextRecordsUrl as a full path. The node keeps only the trailing locator, checks it against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, and rebuilds the path itself, so a cursor coming from a model cannot point the node at another endpoint on the org.
quirks.page_size: Salesforce decides the page size (2000 records for most objects, fewer for wide rows). There is no page-size parameter on this endpoint; use LIMIT in the SOQL to cap the whole result.
